description: Tuwaiq Orbit is a student led team passionate about space exploration, scientific research, and innovation. We aim to develop creative, data driven solutions to real-world challenges using NASA’s open data. We welcome motivated students interested in science, coding, data analysis, and design to join us.
summary:
JD TerraTrace is an environmental intelligence platform that uses NASA Earthdata to reveal hidden changes in Earth’s interconnected systems. Its main innovation is detecting spatial divergence: situations where the same environmental variable changes in opposite directions across different areas, even when the overall regional average appears stable.
The first case study focuses on the Red Sea. The platform compares Sea Surface Temperature (SST) and Chlorophyll-a across northern, central, and southern sectors. Users can explore spatial patterns, view temporal trends, compare variables, and review statistical indicators such as trend direction, change rate, p-values, and confidence information.
JD TerraTrace connects to NASA’s Common Metadata Repository to discover relevant Earth science collections. It also uses official NASA data pathways, including MODIS ocean-color Chlorophyll-a, GHRSST sea-surface temperature, earthaccess, Giovanni, and NASA Harmony.
The current prototype clearly separates live NASA metadata from demonstration analysis values. The next stage will process authenticated NASA data granules with quality filters, spatial masks, temporal aggregation, uncertainty estimation, and statistical validation.
Built with React, TypeScript, and Express, JD TerraTrace is designed to scale beyond the Red Sea to forests, cities, deserts, glaciers, and coastal regions worldwide.
details:
JD TerraTrace is an environmental intelligence platform that uses NASA Earthdata to identify, measure, and explain hidden changes in Earth’s systems. The platform focuses on an important scientific problem: regional averages can hide opposite trends occurring in different locations. For example, one part of a region may be warming while another part is cooling, even though the overall average appears stable.

The first case study focuses on the Red Sea. JD TerraTrace compares Sea Surface Temperature (SST) and Chlorophyll-a across northern, central, and southern sectors. Users can select a sector and explore its spatial signal, time-based trend, estimated rate of change, statistical significance, and relationship with the other variable.

The platform connects to NASA’s Common Metadata Repository (CMR) to discover relevant Earth science data collections. It also documents NASA data pathways including MODIS ocean-color Chlorophyll-a, GHRSST sea-surface temperature, earthaccess, Giovanni, and NASA Harmony. The current prototype clearly separates live NASA metadata from demonstration analysis values. Future versions will process authenticated NASA data granules with quality filters, spatial masks, temporal aggregation, uncertainty estimation, and statistical validation.

JD TerraTrace was developed using React, TypeScript, Express, HTML, CSS, and responsive dashboard design. The prototype uses interactive maps, trend visualizations, relationship plots, and source links to make complex Earth science data easier to understand.

The project is creative because it does not only show whether a variable changed. It also shows where the change happened, whether nearby regions behaved differently, how strong the trend was, and how reliable the result may be. The team considered scientific transparency, data provenance, usability, scalability, statistical uncertainty, and the need to avoid presenting demonstration values as final scientific conclusions.
